thread_a.role: SRCU grace-period work writing the last-GP-end timestamp

thread_b.role: synchronize_srcu caller reading the timestamp locklessly

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([READ srcu_last_gp_end @784]) from thread_b (single-access read that assumes no concurrent conflicting write)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@srcu_gp_end:533 = WRITE ssp->srcu_last_gp_end = ktime_get_mono_fast_ns() (concurrent unmarked write from the GP work)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the timestamp is communicated locklessly across contexts; the reader (task, in srcu_might_be_idle) holds no lock common with the writer (GP delayed work), so no serialize establishes mutual exclusion on the field
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho = atomic(single access) on a scalar broken by a concurrent unsynchronized write -> KCSAN data race (a torn/reordered timestamp read)

fix_maps_to: patch adds WRITE_ONCE(ssp->srcu_last_gp_end, ...) on the write and READ_ONCE() on the read (paired marked accesses). It adds NO lock/serialize/order: it declares the lockless timestamp communication intentional and only prevents tearing/reordering, so it does not 'establish' rho in the {serialize,order,counts} algebra.
recall_risk_notes: Benign single-variable torn-access race on a heuristic timestamp whose ONLY fix is *_ONCE marked accesses -- the torn/reordered-access concern that 4.6.0 places near the weak_memory exclusion. The reader tolerates a stale value (idleness is a heuristic), so there is no real SC ordering invariant or atomic-region intent, just an unmarked-access KCSAN finding. The design deliberately avoids degenerating into a pure syntactic bare-scalar race detector (4.6.3 wants an atomic-primitive guard); with no such guard here it will likely either not raise this or treat it as a borderline/benign precision case. Cross-context pairing (delayed-work process_srcu vs task synchronize_srcu) is itself fine -- surface provides both access paths to the same ssp field. Kept scope=in_scope to match GT type=data_race, but recall is low and it sits on the weak_memory boundary.
